newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai central bank sees baht at 27.50-28.50 vs dlr.
newsitem.headline: Thai central bank sees baht at 27.50-28.50 vs dlr.

text.p: Bank of Thailand Governor Rerngchai Marakanond said on Monday that he saw the baht trading in a 27.50-28.50 range against the U.S. dollar in the future.
His statement follows last week's managed float of the baht by Thai authorities and the setting of a daily baht/dollar reference rate by the central bank.
The central bank said it has an "appropriate level" in mind at which it will intervene in the market to stabilise the baht, but traders have no idea what that level is.
The baht, which lost 15-20 percent of its value on Wednesday after the government announced the flotation, has been relatively steady recently.
Currency trading was quiet as many investors were still trying to digest and understand the new exchange rate system, which they called a de facto devaluation, dealers said.
